A16-12.label: Artist Film (Künstlerroman)
A16-12.defn: A drama of a fictional performer, musician, writer or painter whose art or career is the engine — the artist at work and in crisis (All About Eve, Opening Night, Tár, La belle noiseuse). Films about making films go to Film about Filmmaking; real artists' lives to A11; musicals to A14.
A16-12.axis: by the art: stage, then screen and show-business performers, musicians, writers, and painters and visual artists last

new_leaves.label: Film about Filmmaking
new_leaves.breadth: Fiction films set in the film world: a director, crew or production in crisis
new_leaves.defn: A fiction film whose subject is the making of films — a director's creative crisis, a troubled shoot, the studio or the film world, often self-reflexive (8½, The Bad and the Beautiful, Passion, The State of Things, Day for Night, Pain and Glory, The Fabelmans). Stage and screen performers' careers stay in Artist Film; documentaries on film production go to Making-of Documentary.
new_leaves.aliases: film within a film; metafilm; films about filmmaking; Hollywood-on-Hollywood film
new_leaves.axis: by era: classical and modernist films about filmmaking, the late-modern and festival-auteur decades, then the 2010s onward

A16-23.defn: A drama whose engine is political power — winning and abusing office, or living under it, or communities torn by political conflict (Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Candidate, Yol, Leviathan). Films of militant struggle and revolution go to Revolutionary Film; political thrillers to A3; war to A9.
A16-23.axis: by the relation to power: holding and seeking office, life under repression, then communal conflict and extremism

new_leaves.label: Revolutionary Film
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of militants, uprisings, strikes and revolutionary movements
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is the making of revolution or militant struggle — the activist cell, the uprising, the strike, the liberation movement, often itself made as militant cinema (Wind from the East, Ice, Milestones, Finye, Good Morning, Night, Rang De Basanti). Films of life under a regime without organised resistance stay in Political Drama.
new_leaves.aliases: militant cinema; cinéma militant; revolutionary cinema
new_leaves.axis: by era of the struggle: socialist-realist and early revolutionary films, the 1967–79 militant-cinema wave, then post-1980 activism and uprising

moves: Sjöman's Älskarinnan is an adultery drama, not political
Sjöman's 18th-century sibling-incest drama; no political engine

A19-7.defn: A film that blends documentary and fiction: staged or re-enacted scenes with real people, real people performing scripted or semi-scripted fictions, or fiction shot as documentary (Fires Were Started, Caesar Must Die, Four Daughters, The Arbor). Includes mockumentary features. Docufictions in which a community enacts its own culture go to Ethnofiction.
A19-7.axis: by how fact and fiction are joined: the staged story documentary, re-enactment, the fake documentary, hybrid fiction with non-actors, then the self-reflexive docufiction

new_leaves.label: Ethnofiction
new_leaves.breadth: Docufiction in which a community plays itself within its own culture
new_leaves.defn: A docufiction in which members of a people or community — often indigenous, rural, nomadic or colonised — act out stories in their own setting, language and customs, so that the fiction serves as ethnography (Chang, Louisiana Story, Jaguar, Farrebique, Alamar, The Dead and the Others). Staged films about urban or institutional subjects stay in Docufiction; non-staged fieldwork goes to Ethnographic Film.
new_leaves.axis: by era: the silent and classical staged-ethnography film, Rouch and the ethnofiction of 1960–1999, then contemporary ethnofiction

A19-16.label: Making-of Documentary
A19-16.defn: A documentary about the making of a particular film, series or stage production: the shoot, the rehearsal, the troubled or abandoned project, or the production looked back on (Hearts of Darkness, Burden of Dreams, Lost in La Mancha, Jodorowsky's Dune). Portraits of filmmakers and actors go to Filmmaker Portrait Documentary; histories of cinema to Film History Documentary.
A19-16.axis: by the production's fate and the film's stance: the on-set record, the troubled or unmade production, the retrospective making-of, then the rehearsal film

new_leaves.label: Filmmaker Portrait Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Documentary portraits of directors, actors and other film people
new_leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a person of the cinema — a director, actor, star or craftsperson — built on interviews, archive and the subject's films (Directed by John Ford, Cinéastes de notre temps, Marlene, My Best Fiend, Life Itself, De Palma). The making of one production goes to Making-of Documentary.
new_leaves.aliases: film-director portrait; actor documentary; Cinéastes de notre temps
new_leaves.axis: by the sitter: directors first, then actors and stars, then crew, critics, programmers and archivists

new_leaves.label: Film History Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Documentaries on the history, genres, crafts and criticism of cinema
new_leaves.defn: A documentary that tells the history of cinema or a part of it — a national cinema, studio or era, a genre or cult, the screen image of a group, or a craft or way of watching (The Celluloid Closet, Visions of Light, A Personal Journey with Martin Scorsese Through American Movies, Not Quite Hollywood).
new_leaves.aliases: documentary on film history; cinema history documentary
new_leaves.axis: by the history told: national, studio and industry histories, genre and cult histories, representation on screen, then craft, criticism and cinephilia

A3-21.defn: A film about espionage as tradecraft: agents, moles, defectors and covert operations for a state, played as suspense rather than action spectacle (Notorious, The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, Munich). Gadget-and-stunt superspy films go to Spy-Action Film.
A3-21.axis: by the spy's war: the interwar years and World Wars first, then the Cold War, the covert operation, today's intelligence world; the inter-Korean spy film last

new_leaves.label: Spy-Action Film
new_leaves.breadth: Superspy adventures of gadgets, stunts and global villains
new_leaves.defn: A spy film built as action spectacle: a superspy or agency team, gadgets, chases, exotic locations and a world-threatening villain, usually in a franchise (Dr. No, Goldfinger, Mission: Impossible, The Bourne Identity, Pathaan). Tradecraft and mole-hunt espionage stays in Spy Film.
new_leaves.aliases: superspy film; Bondian film; spy action
new_leaves.axis: by cycle: the James Bond series, its 1960s imitators and the Eurospy wave, the post-Cold War franchises, then the Indian spy universe
secs: Franchise Spy-Action (Bourne, Mission: Impossible, Jack Ryan)

A12-17.defn: A comedy that extracts laughter from death, cruelty, taboo and misfortune, without a political or social target as its main point (Harold and Maude, Happiness, Wild Tales, The Banshees of Inisherin). Comedies whose engine is committing murder go to Murder Comedy; satire of institutions to A12-14 / A12-15 Social Satire.
A12-17.axis: by what the darkness feeds on: death and corpses, misanthropy and taboo, revenge and feuds, escalating nightmare

new_leaves.label: Murder Comedy
new_leaves.breadth: Black comedies whose engine is killing: comic murderers, poisoners and bodies to dispose of
new_leaves.defn: A black comedy built on committing murder — the genteel poisoner, the serial-killing householder, the hapless killer and the body that won't go away, played for laughs (Arsenic and Old Lace, Monsieur Verdoux, Kind Hearts and Coronets, Eating Raoul, Serial Mom, The Green Butchers). Death without a killer stays in Black Comedy; heist-and-crime plots that go wrong to Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy.
new_leaves.axis: by era: the classic murder comedy to 1979, the 1980s–90s cult and suburban killer comedy, then the 21st century

A4-28.defn: A horror film in which a stalking killer murders a group of victims one by one, often till a final girl remains, in the classic cycle from the proto-slashers to the mid-1990s (Black Christmas, Halloween, Friday the 13th, A Nightmare on Elm Street). Slashers after Scream (1996) go to Neo-Slasher; rural killer clans to A4-29; holiday-themed killers to A4-30.
A4-28.axis: by phase of the classic form: proto-slashers, the big franchises, the golden age, supernatural killers

new_leaves.label: Neo-Slasher
new_leaves.breadth: Slasher films after Scream: revival, meta, retro and parody slashers
new_leaves.defn: A slasher film of the cycle that Scream (1996) relaunched: self-aware teen slashers, horror-comedy and time-loop slashers, retro and new-wave throwbacks, and public-domain parody slashers (Scream, I Know What You Did Last Summer, Happy Death Day, X, Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey). Pre-1996 slashers stay in Slasher Film.
new_leaves.axis: by phase: the post-Scream revival, comic, meta and time-loop slashers, retro and new-wave slashers, public-domain parodies

moves: Vigilante (1982) is a vigilante revenge film, no stalk-and-slash
American Dreamer (1984) is a romantic spy-adventure comedy

A4-25.defn: A horror film whose terror lies in the mind: breakdown, grief, trauma, unreal worlds or obsession, with any monster kept ambiguous (Repulsion, Jacob's Ladder, The Babadook, Black Swan). Doubles and split selves go to Doppelgänger Film; horror as social allegory to Social Thriller; a killer stalking victims to A4-28 Slasher Film.
A4-25.axis: by where the horror sits: the unravelling mind, grief and family, purgatory and unreality, obsession and art, confinement

new_leaves.label: Doppelgänger Film
new_leaves.breadth: Horror of doubles, twins, alter egos and split selves
new_leaves.defn: A psychological horror film built on the double: an evil twin, a look-alike, a split personality or an alter ego that takes over (The Other, Dead Ringers, Santa Sangre, Split, Us, Goodnight Mommy).
new_leaves.aliases: double film; evil-twin film; doppelganger horror
new_leaves.axis: by the kind of double: twins and mirror doubles, split personalities and alter egos, then digital and media doubles

new_leaves.label: Social Thriller
new_leaves.breadth: Horror as social allegory of race, gender and class
new_leaves.defn: A horror film that makes a social structure the monster — racism, patriarchy, class or the codes of politeness — in the manner Jordan Peele named with Get Out (Get Out, Antebellum, Master, Nanny, Speak No Evil, The Killing of a Sacred Deer).
new_leaves.axis: by the structure made monstrous: race and its legacy, gender and the body, then class, conformity and social ritual

A12-2.defn: A film built as a vehicle for a solo comedian's established persona, where the performer's routines matter more than the plot (The Bank Dick, The Bellboy, The Gendarme of Saint-Tropez, Wayne's World, Billy Madison). Vehicles for double acts and troupes go to Comedy Team Film; if the film has a stronger premise engine (body swap, heist, parody) it goes there.
A12-2.axis: by the kind of comic persona the film is built around: Hollywood star comedian, national comic persona, sketch character, man-child

new_leaves.label: Comedy Team Film
new_leaves.breadth: Vehicles for double acts and comedy troupes
new_leaves.defn: A comedian comedy built around a double act or comedy team whose established partnership is the attraction (Duck Soup, Sons of the Desert, Road to Morocco, Abbott and Costello Meet Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, Bujang Lapok, Watch Out, We're Mad). Solo comedians' vehicles stay in Comedian Comedy.
new_leaves.aliases: double act film; comedy duo film; comedy troupe film
new_leaves.axis: by era: the studio-era teams, the television-era and national duos of 1960–1989, then contemporary teams

A13-4.label: Adultery Film
A13-4.defn: A love story driven by an affair: a brief or unconsummated encounter, a betrayal of marriage, or a temptation resisted (Brief Encounter, In the Mood for Love, Unfaithful, My Night at Maud's). Two rivals for one heart go to Love Triangle Film; a comic affair to the romantic-comedy leaves.
A13-4.axis: by what the affair does: the brief or unconsummated encounter, adultery and marital betrayal, the temptation tale

new_leaves.label: Love Triangle Film
new_leaves.breadth: Romances of three: two rivals for one heart, or a ménage à trois
new_leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is a triangle — two lovers competing for one person, or three bound together in a ménage à trois — rather than a single affair against a marriage (Bed and Sofa, Two English Girls, César and Rosalie, Sunday Bloody Sunday, Vicky Cristina Barcelona, Heartbeats). Single affairs stay in Adultery Film.
new_leaves.aliases: love-triangle romance; ménage à trois film
new_leaves.axis: by era: the classical triangle, the modernist and New Wave triangle of 1960–1989, then the contemporary triangle
